name: actions/dependency-review-action
what: fails the job when a PR adds vulnerabilities at or above `fail-on-severity`
quote: Defines the threshold for the level of severity. The action will fail on any pull requests that introduce vulnerabilities of the specified severity level or higher.

name: Grype
what: `--fail-on <severity>` exits non-zero on a vulnerability at or above it
quote: set the return code to 2 if a vulnerability is found with a severity >= the given severity, options=%v

name: Syft
what: generates SBOMs and SBOM attestations
quote: **A CLI tool and Go library for generating a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) from container images and filesystems. Exceptional for vulnerability detection when used with a scanner like [Grype](https://github.com/anchore/grype).**

name: srt (Anthropic sandbox-runtime)
what: runs a process tree in an OS sandbox; network denied except allowed domains
quote: **Network Isolation** (allow-only pattern): By default, all network access is denied. You must explicitly allow domains. An empty allowedDomains list means no network access.

name: Trivy
what: `--exit-code` sets the exit status used when issues are found
quote:
By default, `Trivy` exits with code 0 even when security issues are detected.
Use the `--exit-code` option if you want to exit with a non-zero exit code.

name: Bazel sandboxing (linux-sandbox / darwin-sandbox / processwrapper-sandbox)
what: sandboxed actions cannot write outside their sandbox directory; network denial is opt-in
quote:
Linux Namespaces (User, Mount, PID, Network and IPC namespaces) to isolate the
action from the host. That is, it makes the entire filesystem read-only except
for the sandbox directory, so the action cannot accidentally modify anything on
the host filesystem.

name: poutine
what: `--fail-on-violation` exits 10 when any finding is present
quote: --fail-on-violation  Exit with a non-zero code (10) when violations are found

name: cdxgen
what: `cdx-audit` and `cdx-validate` exit 3 on a finding at or above `--fail-severity`
quote: and license policies via `--license-policy`. Non-zero exit codes on findings make it easy to gate CI pipelines. See the [cdx-audit guide](docs/CDX_AUDIT.md) for the full reference.

name: gh attestation verify (GitHub CLI)
what: `gh attestation verify` exits 1 when no attestation verifies against the given policy
quote: - If a command fails for any reason, the exit code will be 1

name: bubblewrap
what: runs a command in new namespaces exposing only the paths the caller binds
quote:
bubblewrap always creates a new mount namespace, and the user can specify
exactly what parts of the filesystem should be visible in the sandbox.
Any such directories you specify mounted `nodev` by default, and can be made readonly.
note: Its `SECURITY.md` says it is not a security boundary between the user and the OS and that protection depends on the arguments passed. It still confines the process it runs.

name: GuardDog
what: its analysis runs in a Landlock or Seatbelt sandbox; `--exit-non-zero-on-finding` is opt-in
quote: GuardDog runs source code analysis inside a **kernel-level sandbox** (Linux via Landlock, macOS via Seatbelt, using [nono](https://github.com/always-further/nono-py)). The sandbox blocks all network access and restricts filesystem operations to only the paths needed for analysis.
note: The sandbox confines the scanner's own analysis, not a consumer's install. The documentation says it is required, and that the scan fails rather than run without it.

name: Deno `--allow-scripts` (npm lifecycle scripts)
what: `deno install` does not run npm lifecycle scripts unless a package is allowed by name
quote:
Unlike npm, Deno does not run these scripts by default as they pose a potential
security vulnerability.

You can still run these scripts by passing the `--allow-scripts=<packages>` flag
when running `deno install`:

name: OWASP Dependency-Check
what: `--failOnCVSS` / `failBuildOnCVSS` fails the build at a CVSS threshold
quote: Specifies if the build should be failed if a CVSS score equal to or above a specified level is identified. The default is 11 which means since the CVSS scores are 0-10, by default the build will never fail.

name: Dependency-Track
what: records policy violations for others to act on; the plugins that fail builds are community-maintained
quote:
The state propagates into project
metrics, project badges, and the [`POLICY_VIOLATION` notification group](../reference/notifications/groups.md).
Organizations typically use a `FAIL` violation to break a CI/CD pipeline.
note: Its documentation says a `FAIL` violation is what organisations use to break a pipeline, and lists every CI plugin that does so as community work not supported by the project.

name: bomber
what: `--exitcode` exits with a code for the highest severity found; marked experimental
quote: Using the flag `--exitcode`, will return with an exit code representing the highest vulnerability severity found. Without this flag you can expect an exit code of `0` for success, or `1` if an error was encountered.

name: Gemini CLI sandbox
what: `--sandbox` runs tools under Seatbelt, in a container, or in a Windows low-integrity sandbox
quote:
**Default profile**: `permissive-open` - denies operations by default; confines
writes to the project directory while allowing broad file reads and network
access.

name: Capslock
what: `-output=compare` against a saved baseline exits 1 when capabilities differ
quote:
// The exit status code is 2 for an error, 1 if a difference is found when a
// comparison is requested, and 0 otherwise.
note: The exit status is documented in the command's package comment, the text `go doc` and pkg.go.dev show; the markdown documentation describes `compare` only as identifying which capabilities changed. [capslock/](capslock/) says the tool "does not claim to be a gate". That write-up examined the default mode and the error path, not the comparison.

name: nsjail
what: runs a command in namespaces with resource limits and an optional seccomp policy
quote: Linux process isolation tool using namespaces, resource limits, and seccomp-bpf syscall filters.

name: OSV-Scanner
what: exits 1 when vulnerabilities are found; its Action fails on them by default
quote:
|    `0`    | Packages were found when scanning, but does not match any known vulnerabilities or findings. |
|    `1`    | Packages were found when scanning, and there are vulnerabilities or findings.                |

name: senv (h5i-dev)
what: installs inside a sandbox with network limited to registries; `run` denies network
quote:
senv resolves and installs dependencies in a staging area containing the
project manifests but none of the project source. Network access is restricted
to package registries and pinned at the network layer.

name: Homebrew 6.x sandbox
what: builds, post-install steps, tests and cask steps run under Seatbelt or Landlock
quote: Homebrew uses sandboxing on macOS and Linux to limit what package processing, builds, supported installation steps and tests can access.

name: in-toto (Python reference implementation)
what: `in-toto-verify` returns 1 when layout verification fails
quote:
The command returns 2 if it is called with wrong arguments, 1 if in-toto
verification fails and 0 if verification passes.

name: in-toto/witness (+ in-toto/go-witness)
what: `witness verify` exits non-zero when attestations fail the signed policy
quote:
`Witness verify` will evaluate a set of attestation collections against a policy document. If the attestation
collections satisfy the policy, Witness will exit with an exit code of 0. Any other exit code indicates an error or
policy failure.

name: sbomqs
what: `sbomqs policy` exits 1 when a policy whose action is `fail` is violated
quote:
- `fail` → Mark the policy as failed (exit code non-zero, block CI/CD pipeline)
- `warn` → Report the violation but continue (exit code zero)

name: mise sandboxing
what: `--deny-*` flags or settings confine a command with Landlock and seccomp, or Seatbelt
quote: Filesystem sandboxing uses [Landlock](https://landlock.io/) (available since Linux 5.13). Network sandboxing uses [seccomp-bpf](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/userspace-api/seccomp_filter.html) to block inet socket creation while allowing Unix sockets.

name: kyverno (verifyImages / ImageValidatingPolicy)
what: admission webhook denies non-compliant images under `Enforce`; `kyverno apply` exits 1 on failures
quote: If the value is set to `Enforce`, resource creation or updates are blocked when the resource does not comply. When the value is set to `Audit`, a policy violation is logged in a `PolicyReport` or `ClusterPolicyReport` but the resource creation or update is allowed.
note: For ClusterPolicy admission the documented default is `Audit`, which only writes a report. `kyverno apply`, part of the same project, exits 1 on failures without a switch.

name: @lavamoat/allow-scripts (LavaMoat)
what: turns lifecycle scripts off and runs only allowlisted ones; exits 1 on a dependency with no policy
quote: `@lavamoat/allow-scripts` increases your project's security posture by first _denying_ all lifecycle scripts from running, then _allowing_ the ones you actually need. The workflow looks like this:

name: Microsoft sbom-tool
what: `validate` exits 3 when a build drop fails validation against its manifest
note: The action classified is `validate`. The defect reported in [sbom-tool/](sbom-tool/) is in `ValidateFormat`, a different one.

name: cplt (navikt)
what: runs a command under Seatbelt, or Landlock and seccomp; denies credential paths and non-443 egress
quote: The sandbox blocks access to credentials and secrets in the kernel. Command guards block destructive operations. Every restriction applies to the agent and to every process it spawns.

name: firejail
what: confines a process tree with namespaces, seccomp and capability drops
quote:
Enable a new, unconnected network namespace. The only interface
available in the new namespace is a new loopback interface (lo).
Use this option to deny
network access to programs that don't really need network access.

name: Nix build sandbox (NixOS/nix)
what: builds run isolated from the host in private namespaces
quote:
If set to `true`, builds are performed in a *sandboxed
          environment*, i.e., they're isolated from the normal file system
          hierarchy and only see their dependencies in the Nix store,

name: nono (nolabs-ai)
what: Landlock or Seatbelt sandbox; blocks paths outside its grants and credential paths
quote: nono wraps any command with an OS-level sandbox. You specify what the command is allowed to access, and nono enforces those restrictions at the kernel level.

name: notation (CLI) + notation-go (library)
what: `notation verify` fails when no signature satisfies the trust policy
quote: to report execution status information about success or failure. Notation returns `EXIT_FAILURE` if and only if Notation reports one or more errors.

name: npm audit signatures / npm provenance verification (npm CLI)
repo: https://github.com/npm/cli — verifier at lib/utils/verify-signatures.js, command at lib/commands/audit.js
tool: npm audit signatures (npm CLI registry-signature and provenance verification)
what: `npm audit signatures` exits 1 on an invalid or missing signature or attestation
quote: This command checks the registry signatures and provenance attestations. If a package has missing or invalid signatures or attestations, it returns an error. This could indicate that a package has been tampered with.

name: OpenAI Codex CLI sandbox
what: commands the model runs are confined by bubblewrap and seccomp, Seatbelt, or a Windows sandbox
quote:
- When bubblewrap is active, the helper applies `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` and a
  seccomp network filter in-process.
- When bubblewrap is active, the filesystem is read-only by default via `--ro-bind / /`.

name: Allstar
what: `action: fix` puts GitHub settings back to the configured state; the default action is `log`
quote:
If Allstar detects a
security policy violation, it creates an issue to alert the repository or
organization owner.  For some security policies, Allstar can also automatically
change the project setting that caused the violation, reverting it to the
expected state.
note: Gates by putting back a setting it was told to hold, not by refusing an action.

name: OSSF package-analysis
what: each analysed package is installed and run in a gVisor sandbox
quote:
Sandboxing via [gVisor](https://gvisor.dev/) containers ensures the packages are
isolated. Detonating a package inside the sandbox allows us to capture strace
note: The sandbox protects the host doing the analysis, not a consumer's install or build. It still confines a process, and the documentation says the packages are isolated, which is a claim of enforcement.

name: OpenSSF Scorecard
what: scores, findings, a badge and a dataset; the project names Allstar as the enforcer
quote:
Scorecard accepts diverse inputs
about a project's security practices, normalizes them through probe-based
analysis, and packages the resulting evidence in interoperable formats for
downstream tools to act on.

name: packj
what: installs under a syscall-interposing sandbox with a copy-on-write layer and a network list
quote: Packj sandbox creates a network firewall and an isolated filesystem layer by interposing on system calls (e.g., `open`, `connect`) with [strace](https://github.com/strace/strace) and re-writing system calls arguments (e.g., file path) as per the sandboxing rules in `.packj.yaml`.

name: OWASP dep-scan
what: `depscan-validate` exits non-zero on an invalid VEX/VDR document; server mode refuses private-address fetches
quote: The command exits with a non-zero status when any document is invalid, which makes it convenient to gate a CI pipeline:
note: The main scan does not exit on vulnerabilities. `depscan-validate` is documented at the pinned commit but was added after the latest release, 6.3.0. Server mode, which is released, refuses by default to fetch URLs that resolve to private or loopback addresses, which also gates; it protects the server.

name: birdcage (Phylum)
what: library that spawns a child with filesystem and network denied except what is granted
quote:
Birdcage is a cross-platform embeddable sandboxing library allowing restrictions
to Filesystem and Network operations using native operating system APIs.

name: projectkennel
what: runs a workload under a signed policy; ungranted paths absent, egress denied by default
quote: **Kennel runs code you haven't vetted — an AI coding agent, an `npm install`, a freshly-cloned repo — under your own user account, confined to just the files, network, and programs a signed policy allows.**

name: protobom
what: library that reads and writes SPDX and CycloneDX
quote: The `protobom` library can be used to read in and write out SBOM documents in any of the above formats.

name: pip-audit
what: exits 1 when a known vulnerability is found
quote:
On completion, `pip-audit` will exit with a code indicating its status.

The current codes are:

* `0`: No known vulnerabilities were detected.
* `1`: One or more known vulnerabilities were found.

name: actionlint
what: exits 1 when it finds a problem in workflow files
quote:
| `0`    | The command ran successfully and no problem was found   |
| `1`    | The command ran successfully and some problem was found |
| `2`    | The command failed due to invalid command line option   |
| `3`    | The command failed due to some fatal error              |

name: pmg (safedep)
what: blocks installs of known-malicious packages; an OS sandbox for installs is opt-in
quote: - **Layer 1: Threat Intelligence** - PMG checks every package against [SafeDep's real-time threat intelligence](https://safedep.io) before install. Known malicious packages are blocked. No key, no login required.

name: ratchet
what: `ratchet lint` exits non-zero when a reference is unpinned
quote:
The `lint` command reports if all versions are pinned, printing any violations,
and exiting with a non-zero error code when entries are not pinned:
note: `pin`, `update` and `upgrade` only rewrite files; the check mode is what gates.

name: sigstore/cosign
what: `verify` commands exit non-zero when verification fails
quote:
| 10 | Error verifying image due to no signature|
| 11 | Error verifying image due to non-existent tag|
| 12 | Error verifying image due to no matching signature|
| 13 | Error verifying image due to no certificate found on signature|

name: sigstore/gitsign
what: `gitsign verify` fails when the signature, log entry or identity check fails
quote:
verify verifies a commit against a set of certificate claims.
This should generally be used over git verify-commit, since verify will
check the identity included in the signature's certificate.
note: The documentation describes `verify` as checking a commit against certificate claims and does not state an exit status.

name: sigstore/policy-controller
what: admission webhook rejects images that fail a policy, in namespaces labelled for it
quote: | mode | Mode controls whether a failing policy will be rejected (not admitted), or if errors are converted to Warnings. enforce - Reject (default) warn - allow but warn | string | false |

name: slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator
what: the container builder's `verify` exits 1 on a mismatch; its download actions fail on a bad hash
quote:
The `verify` subcommand takes the path to a SLSAv1.0 provenance and verifies it,
by rebuilding the artifacts using the build definition in the provenance, and
checking that the resulting artifacts have the same names and subjects as the
ones in the provenance subject.
note: Its main product is provenance for others to verify. Two documented parts of the same repository verify and fail on a mismatch.

name: slsa-framework/slsa-verifier
what: every `verify-*` command exits 1 when provenance verification fails

name: Socket Firewall Free (sfw)
what: proxy that blocks fetches of confirmed-malicious package artifacts
quote: Socket Firewall Free is a lightweight tool that protects developer machines in real time, blocking malicious dependencies before they ever reach your laptop or build system.

name: Socket CLI
what: `socket npm`, `pnpm` and `yarn` install through Socket Firewall, which blocks known-malicious packages
quote:
`socket npm`, `socket pnpm`, and `socket yarn` each run the underlying
package manager through [Socket Firewall](https://docs.socket.dev), which
blocks known-malicious packages before they are installed.

name: Aura
what: documented to exit 1 when the audit checks have not passed
quote:
0    Code scan completed successfully, passing all audit checks
1    An error occurred during the code scan or the audit checks haven't passed
note: Exit 1 is shared with scan errors, and the documentation never says what the audit checks are. It does tie the code to the checks and offers it for CI, and the classification is of what the documentation says.

name: sse-secure-systems/connaisseur
what: admission webhook denies images that fail signature verification; `detectionMode` only warns
quote:
To do so, it intercepts resource creation or update requests sent to the Kubernetes cluster, identifies all container images and verifies their signatures against pre-configured public keys.
Based on the result, it either accepts or denies those requests.

name: StepSecurity Harden-Runner
what: blocks CI runner egress outside allowed endpoints; a global block list applies in audit mode too
quote: Block known-malicious domains and IP addresses tied to active supply chain attacks, maintained by StepSecurity's 24x7 SOC. No configuration required, new indicators apply automatically without an action version bump, and it is enforced even in `egress-policy: audit` mode.
note: The action's input `egress-policy` defaults to `block`, and the global block list needs no configuration; the README's own example sets `audit`. Block mode is Linux only.

name: StepSecurity secure-repo
what: proposes hardened workflow files as a pull request
quote: - View recommendations and click `Create pull request.` Here is an example pull request: https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/36343.

name: pinact
what: `pinact run --check` exits 1 when an action needs pinning; exits 2 on one it cannot fix
quote: The exit code 1 is the one CI is meant to fail on: it says the files aren't pinned, and running pinact without `--fix=false` fixes them.
note: A rewriter with a check mode; the check mode is what gates.

name: octoscan
what: findings as text, JSON or SARIF; its Action uploads the SARIF and ignores the exit status
quote: Security results can the be reviewed in the code security tab if you have write access on the target repository:
note: The source returns exit status 2 when findings exist, but no documentation, help text or Action says so, and the official Action discards the status.

name: Tern
what: writes SBOM reports for container images
quote: Tern creates a report containing the Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) of a container image, including notes about how it collects this information, and files for which it has no information about.

name: zizmor
what: exits 11 to 14 by the highest severity found
quote: | 14   | One or more findings found; highest finding is "high" level. |

name: landrun (Zouuup)
what: Landlock sandbox that denies filesystem and TCP access not granted
quote: If no paths or network rules are specified and neither unrestricted flag is set, landrun will apply maximum restrictions (denying all access)

name: Fence
repo: Named in the already-assessed list; canonical repository not re-established here by design.
what: runs a command in an OS sandbox; network and writes denied unless allowed
quote: Fence wraps commands in a sandbox that blocks network access by default and restricts filesystem operations based on configurable rules.
